message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 121, "amount_cents": 5261}, {"order_id": 122, "amount_cents": 5470}, {"order_id": 124, "amount_cents": 1085}]
Refunds requested in this batch (from the batch order, signed by Alpha): [{"order_id": 121, "amount_cents": 5261}, {"order_id": 122, "amount_cents": 5470}, {"order_id": 124, "amount_cents": 1085}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I should verify the handoff by checking the orders and refunds on the shared ledger rather than trusting W2's message alone.
The refunds on the ledger match what W2 reported and what was requested. Next I'll check the orders so I can confirm the refunds apply to real orders before computing any payouts.
The refunds on the ledger match W2's report and the signed batch, and all three refunded orders exist. Next I'll get each customer's net balance from the ledger, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance is 31368 cents. Acme has no refunds, and its orders total 5706 + 25662 = 31368, which matches. Next I'll get birch's net balance.

Birch's ledger net of 14737 matches my check: orders 8002 + 13081 = 21083, minus refunds 5261 + 1085 = 6346. Next I'll get cobalt's net balance, which has one refund (order 122) and should come to 29756 - 5470 = 24286.
All three net balances match my independent check against the orders and refunds, so the figures are verified. I'll record the first payout, for acme, at 31368 cents.
Acme's payout is recorded. Birch's net balance of 14737 matches my independent check, so I'll record that payout next.
Cobalt's ledger net of 24286 matches my independent check (orders 7562 + 22194 = 29756, minus refund 5470). Acme and birch are already paid, so I'll record cobalt's payout now.
All three payouts are recorded and each matched my independent check against the orders and refunds. The batch is complete.
